name: remote-desktop
description: A Linux desktop streamed into a tab as low-latency video (AV1, H.265 or H.264 from the GPU where the host has one) with full keyboard, mouse, clipboard, cursor and audio; a managed virtual desktop follows the tab's size and scale, or attach to an existing X11 or Wayland desktop. Powered by QuickRemote; its host downloads from the project's releases with one click.

enumItemLabels: Managed display (virtual desktop that follows the tab)
remoteDesktop.mode.description: Managed: start a virtual display (headless sway) with a desktop session on it, and let the desktop follow the tab's size and scale. Existing: attach to the desktop already running on this machine (Wayland: KDE, GNOME or wlroots; else X11); input goes to that real screen and its size is never changed. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.display.description: Existing mode only: an X display to attach to, e.g. ":0". Leave empty to detect the running desktop (Wayland or X11).

remoteDesktop.desktopCommand.description: Managed mode only: the command that starts the desktop environment (e.g. xfce4-session, startlxde, mate-session), run on a rootful Xwayland inside the virtual display. Must be installed on the host.

remoteDesktop.useGlobalConfig.description: Managed mode only: run the desktop with your own config directory (~/.config) instead of a fresh one each Start, so your theme, panel and window manager settings apply and changes made on the virtual desktop are kept. If the same desktop also runs on this machine's screen at the same time, both sessions share those files. Needs qr-host 0.2.1 or newer. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.keyboardLayout.description: Managed mode only: XKB layout for the virtual display, e.g. us, de, fr. Keys are forwarded by physical position, so this should match the keyboard you type on.

enumItemLabels: Auto (GPU when a render node is usable)
remoteDesktop.renderer.description: Managed mode only: how the virtual display renders apps. GPU uses a render node (/dev/dri/renderD*, which needs the render group) so OpenGL, Vulkan and WebGL apps run on it; software renders in pixman and encodes on the CPU. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.port.description: Preferred loopback port for the stream. If it is taken, the next free port is used.

remoteDesktop.fps.description: Frame rate cap. A still screen costs almost nothing regardless. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.bitrateKbps.description: Upper bitrate limit in kilobits per second. The stream adapts below it when the connection struggles, and the viewer's quality preset caps it further. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.codec.description: Video codec for the stream. Every tab and device viewing the desktop shares one stream, so Auto keeps it on H.264; H.265 or AV1 look sharper at the same bitrate, but each viewing browser must decode them (one that can't shows "No common codec"). Needs qr-host 0.2.1 or newer for anything but Auto. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.pixelRatio.description: Default remote pixels per CSS pixel for your devices. Auto detects each device's pixel ratio (capped at 2, so a 3x phone gets a 2x desktop). Each browser can override this for itself from the viewer tab's view settings; the desktop follows the ratio of the tab that drives it.

remoteDesktop.dpi.description: Managed mode only: font DPI reported to apps on the virtual display.

remoteDesktop.serverPath.description: Path to your own qr-host build. Leave empty to use the one downloaded from the Remote Desktop panel (kept in ~/.local/share/perch-remote-desktop), then PATH, then ~/.cargo/bin.
